beliefs.practice: Read the cluster connection string only from an environment variable (e.g., DOCUMENTDB_URI) at runtime and never commit secrets to source control; provide a .env.example with a placeholder instead.
Enforce TLS/SSL on client connections (e.g., use tls=true / ssl=true in the Mongo URI) and verify server certificate to protect credentials and data-in-flight.
Use a least-privilege account or scoped key for application access and rotate keys regularly; avoid using the account's master key for day-to-day app access.
Tune connection pool parameters (e.g., maxPoolSize/minPoolSize, maxIdleTimeMS) in the Mongo driver to match expected concurrency and avoid connection storms.
Set sensible timeouts (serverSelectionTimeoutMS, connectTimeoutMS, socketTimeoutMS) so application requests fail fast on network issues instead of hanging indefinitely.
Enable and implement exponential-backoff retries for transient errors (with idempotency for writes) and consider enabling driver retryWrites if supported by the cluster.
Use bulkWrite / bulk upsert for seeding and large ingest operations rather than many single upserts to reduce round-trips and improve throughput.
Keep documents small and bounded (well under the 16MB MongoDB document limit); for product catalogs, store assets externally (CDN/blob) and only keep metadata + embeddings in the document.
Create and maintain a text index over user-facing text fields used for $text search (e.g., name, description) and set field weights for BM25-style ranking (text index weights).

Create or configure a vector index using the cluster's supported index type (DiskANN/HNSW/IVF) and tune core parameters (e.g., M, efConstruction/efSearch, metric) appropriate to dimensionality and latency/accuracy tradeoffs.

Store embeddings as a fixed-length numeric array (Float32/float list) with consistent dimensionality across all documents and, when using cosine similarity, store normalized (unit) vectors so distances/scores are comparable.

When combining BM25 ($text) and vector scores (hybrid/RRF), normalize both score ranges before fusion and document the fusion formula; prefer Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF) or min-max scaling + weighted sum.
For common filter + sort query patterns create compound indexes that match the query's predicate and sort order to avoid collection scans (e.g., {category:1, price:1}).
Use projections to return only needed fields (e.g., exclude embeddings from search results by default) to minimize network IO and quota/throughput usage.
Use pagination patterns that avoid large skip costs (use range queries or seek-based (bookmark) pagination keyed on a stable sort-field) instead of skip/limit for deep paging.
Run explain() on representative queries (text search, vector search + fuse queries) to confirm index usage and to tune indexes and query plans before shipping.

Provision sufficient cluster resources / instance size (e.g., compute tier M30 or equivalent) and index RU/IO budget for vector indexes; monitor RU/throughput and scale provisioned capacity or cluster size as query volume grows.
Instrument and monitor key metrics (op latency, RU consumption, index build progress, cache hit rate, failed queries, connection counts) and set alerts for sustained high latency or RU throttling.

Sanitize and validate user inputs used in regex or raw query construction (escape regex meta-characters, set anchored patterns, and/or cap execution time) to prevent denial-of-service or excessive scanning.
Cache expensive or repeated embeddings locally (or in a fast cache) to avoid repeated calls to external embedding services; treat embedding generation as an idempotent, memoized operation.

When building vector indexes on a live cluster, build during low-traffic windows or use online/rolling index-build features if available; monitor index-build resource usage to avoid impacting queries.
Set a query execution timeout (maxTimeMS) for user-initiated searches so a single expensive search cannot saturate the cluster.
Choose an appropriate collation (case-insensitive or language-specific) on the collection or per-query when you need consistent case/locale behavior for text matching.
Avoid embedding very large arrays or frequently-updated growing arrays inside documents (they cause document churn and index pressure); model 1:N relationships in separate collections when necessary.

Sanity-check index and query support for MongoDB wire-protocol features you rely on (e.g., $text, $search, vector operators) against the target cluster version and the MCP server tools before assuming behavior identical to upstream MongoDB.
